sentences.text: Huanghetitan was a basal titanosauriform, an early member of the group that includes giant long-necked dinosaurs, living in what is now Gansu, China.
In 2019, Gregory S. Paul suggested that the species H. ruyangensis could have weighed between 45 and 55 metric tons based on comparisons with Patagotitan.
The type species Huanghetitan liujiaxiaensis was described by You et al. in 2006 from fragmentary fossils found in the Lanzhou Basin, Gansu Province, in 2004.
A second species, H. ruyangensis, was described in 2007 from fossils found in Ruyang County, Henan Province.
A family named Huangetitanidae was proposed for Huanghetitan in 2007, but later analyses found it to be polyphyletic, meaning its members do not share a single exclusive common ancestor.

Huanghetitan lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 125 and 89 million years ago, in what is now Asia. The time range for Huanghetitan is estimated from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
Recent cladistic analysis suggests H. ruyangensis is unlikely to be closely related to H. liujiaxiaensis and may require a new genus name.
